_notes.volume: Attach a Railway volume to this service with mount path /data — SQLite needs a real filesystem, and a single replica owns it. The Dockerfile declares no VOLUME (Railway rejects builds that do) and no USER: the container starts as root only to chown the mount, which arrives root-owned, then entrypoint.sh re-execs itself as uid 10001.
_notes.replicas: Keep numReplicas at 1. Two web replicas on one volume would each open the same SQLite files.
_notes.storage: The same four R2 credentials serve two jobs: Litestream ships control.db continuously, and app/storage/r2_sync.py snapshots each tenant database after a write. R2_ENDPOINT_URL and R2_ENDPOINT are interchangeable — set either and both consumers read it.
_notes.scaling: Stage 2+: MAX_LOCAL_TENANTS caps tenant files on local disk (0 = unlimited), and BRAIN_SHARD_INDEX/BRAIN_SHARD_TOTAL plus BRAIN_SHARD_URLS or BRAIN_SHARD_INSTANCES spread tenants across nodes. Both default to off, and both need R2 configured.
_notes.proxy: Railway terminates TLS and forwards plain HTTP. The entrypoint runs uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=* so the app sees the real scheme and client address, and BRAIN_PUBLIC_URL must be the https origin clients will use — every discovery document is built from it.
_notes.models: LLM_API_KEY (or ZAI_API_KEY) powers extraction, vision and embeddings. The embedding default for a Z.ai base URL is `embedding-3`, which api.z.ai rejects with 400 'Unknown Model' — it is a bigmodel.cn id. Point embeddings at a host that serves them: EMBEDDING_BASE_URL + EMBEDDING_MODEL, or DASHSCOPE_API_KEY to move them to Alibaba's Qwen3 endpoint. Run `python -m app.cli doctor --probe` after any change: it calls the hosts instead of trusting the names.
_notes.audience: BRAIN_AUDIENCE is optional and now defaults to BRAIN_PUBLIC_URL + /mcp. Set it only to pin a different RFC 8707 resource identifier.
